newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end one percent higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end one percent higher.

text.p: Swiss shares closed one percent higher after a firming Wall Street supported the indices in late trade.
The easing Swiss franc was favourable for industrials, dealers said. A techical reaction to Friday's losses buoyed shares from the start, but some profit taking temporarily put prices under pressure.
"People do not want to take chances ahead of the year's end", a trader noted. Volumes sagged towards the end of the session.
Further development was seen depending on Wall Street.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index was up 38.5 points, or one percent, to 3,874.0.
Power utility and industrial group Elektrowatt stood out among blue chips with an advance of six percent, or 29 francs, to 511.

The stock thrived on a press report CS Holding was ready to sell its 45 percent stake in Electrowatt immediately. Dealers said there were rumours that CS Holding may sell its stake before the end of the year.
A CS Holding spokesman did not comment on the speculations and repeated CS Holding was ready to sell its stake in due time. "Due time means the right buyer and the right price", he said.
Most-active Roche certificates soared 1.66 percent to 10,075 francs on a positive study and buy recommendations.
Ciba and Sandoz profited from rumours the approval of U.S. authorities to form Novartis may come soon. Ciba registered shares advanced 1,13 persent to 1,616 francs. Sandoz were up 14 francs to 1,516.
ABB added 1.1 percent to 1,648. Sulzer added almost three percent to 743 francs.
The recovery in financials was not as marked as in industrials, dealers said.
CS Holding and insurer Swiss Re both climbed more than one percent to 135 francs and 1,408 francs, respectively. Insurer Baloise was up 40 francs to 2,900.
